name: Congenital Systemic Veins Anomaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Congenital Systemic Veins Anomaly Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of abnormal systemic venous connections demonstrated by imaging
Absence or hypoplasia of normal systemic veins such as the superior or inferior vena cava
Coexisting congenital cardiac malformations identified clinically or by imaging

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least two major criteria including abnormal systemic venous connections and absence or hypoplasia of normal systemic veins
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on detailed imaging studies such as echocardiography, CT angiography, or MRI.

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible elevated liver enzymes if congestion present
imaging: Echocardiography showing abnormal systemic venous return
CT angiography or MRI demonstrating venous anomalies
Venography confirming absence or interruption of vena cava
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be associated with syndromic congenital heart diseases

distinguishingFeatures: Pulmonary veins drain into systemic venous circulation rather than left atrium
More severe cyanosis and heart failure in neonates
Isolated persistent left superior vena cava without interruption of inferior vena cava

redFlags: Severe cyanosis in neonate or infant
Signs of venous congestion such as hepatomegaly or peripheral edema
